html: // canvas_app_runner — the browser half of canvas_apps, and the twin of // native/CanvasAppRunner.roc. It loads an app's wasm, runs the clock and the // keyboard, and hands each frame to ShapesCanvas to paint. // // Not every program built against this file is a game: `camera` is a world // you fly around and `trick_or_treat` is a movie you can scrub. What they // share is that each is a Roc value on a canvas, stepped at its own rate and // drawn from what it answers. The `game` in the names below is older than // that. // // The app is the same Roc that runs natively. What is in here is only what a // browser does differently: keep the input, pace the clock, show the speaker. // Reading a frame and filling a canvas is shapes_canvas.js, which this loads // first and which knows nothing about any of them. // // window.SHOW = { wasm: 'snake.wasm', loading: '…', readsPointer: true } // // A page that sets `sharp: true` keeps one canvas pixel for each pixel of the // screen, however the page has scaled the canvas, so its type stays crisp. // // A page that opens partway lists the words its address may name, as // `opensAt: ['trees', 'grass']`, and `?start=grass` opens it at the second. // // No hint: every game draws the keys it reads in its own HUD, which is the // only place that cannot drift from the keys it actually reads. // ── the keyboard ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── // The page owns it and the game is told. Every tick carries two bit sets: // which keys are down now, and which went down since the last tick. A game // needs both — snake turns on the edge, a paddle moves while a key is held — // so an event alone will not do. // // The bits are Keys.roc's, and safari/gates/input_bits.shale holds the two equal. const KEY_BIT = { ArrowUp: 1, ArrowDown: 2, ArrowLeft: 4, ArrowRight: 8, KeyW: 16, KeyA: 32, KeyS: 64, KeyD: 128, Space: 256, Enter: 512, KeyP: 1024, KeyR: 2048, KeyQ: 4096, KeyE: 8192, KeyC: 16384, Digit1: 32768, Digit2: 65536, Digit3: 131072, Digit4: 262144, KeyJ: 524288, }; const maskOf = (codes) => [...codes].reduce((bits, code) => bits | (KEY_BIT[code] ?? 0), 0); function watchKeyboard(target) { const held = new Set(); let struck = new Set(); // A shortcut belongs to the browser: Ctrl+R reloads, Ctrl+F finds. const known = (event) => event.code in KEY_BIT && !(event.ctrlKey || event.metaKey || event.altKey); target.addEventListener('keydown', (event) => { if (!known(event)) return; if (!event.repeat) struck.add(event.code); held.add(event.code); event.preventDefault(); }); target.addEventListener('keyup', (event) => { if (!known(event)) return; held.delete(event.code); event.preventDefault(); }); // A window that loses focus loses its keys with it, or a paddle sticks. target.addEventListener('blur', () => { held.clear(); struck.clear(); }); // Reading a snapshot consumes the edges, as one tick's worth. return () => { const snapshot = { held: maskOf(held), struck: maskOf(struck) }; struck = new Set(); return snapshot; }; } // ── the pointer ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── // A mouse, a finger and a pen all arrive as pointer events, so an app can't // tell them apart. Position is reported in the game's own coordinates, so a // game never learns how big the window is or how the page scaled the canvas. // During a drag it may be off the canvas. // `event.buttons` uses Mouse.roc's bits, and safari/gates/input_bits.shale holds the // two equal, as it does KEY_BIT. const MOUSE_BIT = { Left: 1, Right: 2, Middle: 4 }; const MOUSE_BITS = MOUSE_BIT.Left | MOUSE_BIT.Right | MOUSE_BIT.Middle; function watchPointer(canvas, width, height) { let held = 0; let struck = 0; let at = { x: 0, y: 0 }; let wheel = 0; // The pointer that pressed on the canvas, until it lets go. A second finger // is ignored until then. let dragger = null; const place = (event) => { const box = canvas.getBoundingClientRect(); at = { x: ((event.clientX - box.left) / box.width) * width, y: ((event.clientY - box.top) / box.height) * height, }; }; const readButtons = (event) => { const now = event.buttons & MOUSE_BITS; struck |= now & ~held; held = now; }; const release = (event) => { if (event.pointerId !== dragger) return; held = 0; dragger = null; }; canvas.addEventListener('pointerdown', (event) => { if (dragger !== null && event.pointerId !== dragger) return; dragger = event.pointerId; // With capture, a drag that leaves the canvas keeps tracking and ends here. canvas.setPointerCapture(dragger); place(event); readButtons(event); event.preventDefault(); }); canvas.addEventListener('pointermove', (event) => { if (dragger !== null && event.pointerId !== dragger) return; place(event); // A mouse's other buttons arrive as moves: pointerdown and pointerup come // only with the first button down and the last one up. if (dragger !== null) readButtons(event); }); canvas.addEventListener('pointerup', release); canvas.addEventListener('pointercancel', release); canvas.addEventListener('contextmenu', (event) => event.preventDefault()); // Positive is away from the hand, as raylib reports it; a browser's deltaY // is the other way round. canvas.addEventListener('wheel', (event) => { wheel -= Math.sign(event.deltaY); event.preventDefault(); }); window.addEventListener('blur', () => { held = 0; struck = 0; dragger = null; }); return () => { const pointer = { held, struck, x: at.x, y: at.y, wheel }; struck = 0; wheel = 0; return pointer; }; } // ── the speaker ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── // The game says a sound happened and what it sounds like; this plays it and // lights a pip. A browser will not start audio until the page has been // clicked or typed in, so the context is made on the first key or button and // the pips work either way. A finger counts only when it lifts, so `wake` runs // again then and resumes a context its pointerdown left suspended. const FADE_MS = 420; const bitsOf = (word) => [...Array(32).keys()].filter((bit) => word & (1 << bit)); // One oscillator per sound, gated to nothing quickly enough not to click. function makeSpeaker(game) { let audio = null; const tones = [...Array(game.toneCount()).keys()].map((i) => ({ freq: game.toneFreq(i), seconds: game.toneMs(i) / 1000, })); const wake = () => { if (typeof AudioContext === 'undefined') return; audio ??= new AudioContext(); audio.resume(); }; const play = (which) => { if (!audio) return; for (const index of which) { const tone = tones[index]; if (!tone) continue; const osc = audio.createOscillator(); const gain = audio.createGain(); osc.frequency.value = tone.freq; gain.gain.setValueAtTime(0.18, audio.currentTime); gain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.001, audio.currentTime + tone.seconds); osc.connect(gain).connect(audio.destination); osc.start(); osc.stop(audio.currentTime + tone.seconds); } }; return { wake, play, count: tones.length }; } function drawSpeaker(ctx, width, height, toneCount, ringing, now) { const age = now - ringing.at; if (age > FADE_MS) return; const fade = 1 - age / FADE_MS; const x = width - 30 - toneCount * 9; const y = height - 26; ctx.save(); ctx.globalAlpha = 0.3 + 0.7 * fade; ctx.fillStyle = '#d7e3ff'; ctx.fillRect(x - 9, y - 4, 5, 8); ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(x - 4, y - 4); ctx.lineTo(x + 2, y - 9); ctx.lineTo(x + 2, y + 9); ctx.lineTo(x - 4, y + 4); ctx.closePath(); ctx.fill(); // One pip per tone the game has; the ones that just sounded are lit. for (let tone = 0; tone < toneCount; tone++) { ctx.fillStyle = ringing.tones.includes(tone) ? '#7ef7d1' : '#2a3566'; ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(x + 14 + tone * 9, y, 3, 0, Math.PI * 2); ctx.fill(); } ctx.restore(); } // ── the page ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── // What the wasm module must provide, checked once so a missing or mismatched // export says which, rather than surfacing later as a bare `unreachable` or as // `Cannot read properties of undefined`. const WANTED = ['memory', 'computeFrame', 'advance', 'sounds', 'toneCount', 'toneFreq', 'toneMs', 'width', 'height', 'fps']; function bindApp(exports) { const missing = WANTED.filter((name) => !(name in exports)); if (missing.length) throw new Error(`canvas_app_runner: the module exports no ${missing.join(', ')}`); if (exports.advance.length !== 7) { throw new Error(`canvas_app_runner: advance takes ${exports.advance.length} arguments, expected 7`); } return { ...exports, // The tick's input arrives as named fields, and this is the one call that // puts them in the export's order. safari/gates/input_bits.shale holds // that order to host.zig's and lib/WasmApp.roc's. advance: ({ key_held, key_struck, button_held, button_struck, x, y, wheel }) => exports.advance(key_held, key_struck, button_held, button_struck, x, y, wheel), // `computeFrame` is the effect, and it answers the address of the Roc // list that holds the frame. RocGlue's reader, generated from the // compiler's type table, turns that list into shapes. // // The view is made after the call, on its own line. Asking for the frame // allocates, which can grow wasm memory, which detaches every DataView // over the old buffer. Written as one expression, // `read(new DataView(memory.buffer), computeFrame())`, JavaScript // evaluates left to right and builds the view first, so the page dies on // the frame that happens to grow memory. frame: () => { const computeStart = performance.now(); const at = exports.computeFrame(); const decodeStart = performance.now(); const shapes = RocGlue.frame(new DataView(exports.memory.buffer), at); FRAME_SPLIT.computeMs = decodeStart - computeStart; FRAME_SPLIT.decodeMs = performance.now() - decodeStart; return shapes; }, }; } const CATCH_UP = 4; // steps one animation frame may take before time is dropped // The last frame's time in the wasm (computing its shapes), in the glue // (decoding them out of the wasm's memory) and on the canvas (painting them), // for the timing log. const FRAME_SPLIT = { computeMs: 0, decodeMs: 0, paintMs: 0 }; // With `?timing=1` in the address, the first frames' times go to the console: // how long the wasm took to load and compile and to take its opening presses, // then per frame the gap since the last one, the steps taken, and the // milliseconds spent stepping and drawing. Comparing the first TIMED_WINDOW of // the TIMED_FRAMES frames with the last tells a slow start (the engine still on // its first, unoptimized code) from a slow ride. Without it nothing is // recorded. const TIMED_FRAMES = 120; const TIMED_WINDOW = 30; function frameTimer() { if (new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('timing') !== '1') return null; const rows = []; const first = [0, TIMED_WINDOW]; const last = [TIMED_FRAMES - TIMED_WINDOW, TIMED_FRAMES]; return { loaded: (ms) => console.log(`canvas_app_runner: wasm loaded, compiled and through its opening presses in ${ms.toFixed(0)} ms`), frame: (row) => { if (rows.length >= TIMED_FRAMES) return; rows.push(row); if (rows.length < TIMED_FRAMES) return; console.table(rows); const slow = (from, to) => rows.slice(from, to).filter((r) => r.stepMs + r.drawMs > 16).length; const mean = (from, to, key) => (rows.slice(from, to).reduce((sum, r) => sum + r[key], 0) / (to - from)).toFixed(1); const steps = (from, to) => rows.slice(from, to).reduce((sum, r) => sum + r.steps, 0); console.log( `canvas_app_runner: frames over 16 ms of work: first ${TIMED_WINDOW} ${slow(...first)}, ` + `last ${TIMED_WINDOW} ${slow(...last)}; ` + `mean step ms ${mean(...first, 'stepMs')} then ${mean(...last, 'stepMs')}, ` + `mean draw ms ${mean(...first, 'drawMs')} then ${mean(...last, 'drawMs')} ` + `(wasm ${mean(...first, 'computeMs')} then ${mean(...last, 'computeMs')}, ` + `decode ${mean(...first, 'decodeMs')} then ${mean(...last, 'decodeMs')}, ` + `paint ${mean(...first, 'paintMs')} then ${mean(...last, 'paintMs')}), ` + `steps taken ${steps(...first)} then ${steps(...last)}`, ); }, }; } // How many times the app hears Right before its first frame: the place in // `opensAt` of the word the address names. An app has no way to hear an address, // so it hears the keys a reader would press to get there. function pressesToOpen(show) { const word = new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('start'); if (word === null) return 0; const presses = (show.opensAt ?? []).indexOf(word); if (presses < 0) throw new Error(`canvas_app_runner: this page can't start at ${word}`); return presses; } async function main(show) { document.body.style.cssText = 'margin:0;background:#06080f;height:100vh;display:flex;flex-direction:column;' + 'align-items:center;justify-content:center;font:13px system-ui,sans-serif;color:#6d7aa8'; const loading = document.createElement('div'); loading.textContent = show.loading ?? 'Loading…'; document.body.appendChild(loading); const timer = frameTimer(); const loadStart = performance.now(); const { instance } = await WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming(fetch(show.wasm), { env: {} }); const game = bindApp(instance.exports); const width = game.width(); const height = game.height(); const toneCount = game.toneCount(); const stepMs = 1000 / game.fps(); const canvas = document.createElement('canvas'); canvas.width = width; canvas.height = height; // A sharp canvas's own size follows the screen, so its place on the page is // said outright: the same one the other canvases get from their own size. canvas.style.cssText = 'background:#06080f;' + (show.sharp ? `width:min(${width}px,100%,${(88 * width) / height}vh);height:auto;aspect-ratio:${width}/${height}` : 'max-width:100%;max-height:88vh'); // A finger on a canvas that reads the pointer is a drag. On any other canvas // it is the reader scrolling the page. canvas.style.touchAction = show.readsPointer ? 'none' : 'auto'; const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d'); const keyboard = watchKeyboard(window); const pointer = watchPointer(canvas, width, height); const speaker = makeSpeaker(game); window.addEventListener('keydown', speaker.wake); window.addEventListener('pointerdown', speaker.wake); window.addEventListener('pointerup', speaker.wake); const ringing = { at: -Infinity, tones: [] }; const step = (now) => { const keys = keyboard(); const mouse = pointer(); game.advance({ key_held: keys.held, key_struck: keys.struck, button_held: mouse.held, button_struck: mouse.struck, x: mouse.x, y: mouse.y, wheel: mouse.wheel, }); const rung = game.sounds(); if (rung) { ringing.at = now; ringing.tones = bitsOf(rung); speaker.play(ringing.tones); } }; // How many canvas pixels the app's pixel takes this frame. Setting a canvas's // size clears it and its transform, so only a change of size sets it. const matchScreen = () => { const across = Math.round(canvas.getBoundingClientRect().width * (window.devicePixelRatio ?? 1)); if (across > 0 && across !== canvas.width) { canvas.width = across; canvas.height = Math.round((across * height) / width); } const scale = canvas.width / width; ctx.setTransform(scale, 0, 0, scale, 0, 0); return scale; }; const draw = (now) => { const scale = show.sharp ? matchScreen() : 1; // The canvas keeps what was drawn, so a frame starts from nothing — // as the native runner's clear does. ctx.globalCompositeOperation = 'source-over'; ctx.fillStyle = '#000'; ctx.fillRect(0, 0, width, height); const shapes = game.frame(); const paintStart = performance.now(); ShapesCanvas.paint(ctx, shapes, scale); FRAME_SPLIT.paintMs = performance.now() - paintStart; drawSpeaker(ctx, width, height, toneCount, ringing, now); }; // The app sets the rate, not the display: elapsed time is banked and steps // are taken as they fall due. let owed = 0; let last = performance.now(); const tick = (now) => { const gap = now - last; owed = Math.min(owed + gap, stepMs * CATCH_UP); last = now; let stepped = 0; const stepStart = performance.now(); while (owed >= stepMs) { step(now); owed -= stepMs; stepped++; } const drawStart = performance.now(); if (stepped) draw(now); timer?.frame({ gapMs: +gap.toFixed(1), steps: stepped, stepMs: +(drawStart - stepStart).toFixed(1), drawMs: +(performance.now() - drawStart).toFixed(1), computeMs: stepped ? +FRAME_SPLIT.computeMs.toFixed(1) : 0, decodeMs: stepped ? +FRAME_SPLIT.decodeMs.toFixed(1) : 0, paintMs: stepped ? +FRAME_SPLIT.paintMs.toFixed(1) : 0, }); }; // A loop that re-arms itself last stops dead on a throw, and this one // clears to black before it decodes, so an uncaught error would leave the // page black and silent. So each tick's error stops the page with its // message: an unknown brush mode, a Roc crash arriving as `unreachable`. // `main`'s catch can't help, because it settled at startup. const loop = (now) => { try { tick(now); } catch (error) { stopped(error); return; } requestAnimationFrame(loop); }; const stopped = (error) => { canvas.remove(); document.body.textContent = `${show.wasm} stopped: ${error.message}`; throw error; // and again into the console, with its stack }; for (let press = pressesToOpen(show); press > 0; press--) { game.advance({ key_held: 0, key_struck: KEY_BIT.ArrowRight, button_held: 0, button_struck: 0, x: 0, y: 0, wheel: 0 }); } timer?.loaded(performance.now() - loadStart); loading.remove(); document.body.appendChild(canvas); try { draw(performance.now()); } catch (error) { stopped(error); return; } last = performance.now(); requestAnimationFrame(loop); } const show = window.SHOW; if (!show) throw new Error('canvas_app_runner: the page did not set window.SHOW'); // A failure here used to leave the loading line up with the reason in the // console, which is the one thing a blank page never tells you. main(show).catch((error) => { document.body.textContent = `${show.wasm} did not start: ${error.message}`; });

name: canvas_apps/web/shapes_canvas.js
html: // shapes_canvas.js paints a frame's shapes onto a browser canvas, for every // canvas app. The shapes are lib/Shapes.roc's `Shape`, which the platform names // as what a frame is; roc_glue.js, generated by `roc glue` from // that type, reads them out of the wasm, and this file does what a canvas // does with them. It answers one name, `ShapesCanvas`, with `paint`. // // Its Roc twin is safari/gates/proof/ShapesPixels.roc, which paints the same shapes into // exact pixels, with no anti-aliasing, for Safari's gate. The gate checks the // twin, not this file, since Roc can't run a canvas. This file is checked by // page_check.mjs, which runs every built page against a stand-in canvas, and // by camera_check.mjs, which checks where a view mark puts points, and by // text_check.mjs, which checks how a line of type is set. const stopAt = (offset, floor = 0) => Math.max(floor, Math.min(1, offset)); const channel = (v) => Math.max(0, Math.min(255, Math.round(v))); const cssColor = (c) => `rgba(${channel(c.r)},${channel(c.g)},${channel(c.b)},${c.a})`; const withStops = (gradient, stops) => { stops.forEach(([offset, color]) => gradient.addColorStop(offset, color)); return gradient; }; // Brush.mix, operation for operation, so a colour's last bit agrees with lib's. const mix = (p, q, t) => ({ r: p.r + (q.r - p.r) * t, g: p.g + (q.g - p.g) * t, b: p.b + (q.b - p.b) * t, a: p.a + (q.a - p.a) * t, }); // Brush's two_stop: the colour the stops give at t, for t in [0, 1]. const twoStopAt = (s, t) => t <= s.start_offset ? s.start_color : t >= s.end_offset ? s.end_color : mix(s.start_color, s.end_color, (t - s.start_offset) / (s.end_offset - s.start_offset)); // A canvas takes offsets in [0, 1] only. An offset past either end becomes a // stop at that end in the colour Brush.shade gives there, so the gradient // matches lib's mix across the whole of [0, 1]. const twoStops = (s) => [ [stopAt(s.start_offset), cssColor(s.start_offset >= 0 ? s.start_color : twoStopAt(s, 0))], [stopAt(s.end_offset, stopAt(s.start_offset)), cssColor(s.end_offset <= 1 ? s.end_color : twoStopAt(s, 1))], ]; // A fill becomes something canvas can paint with. An ellipse is the exception: // it paints through a transform, so it stays a descriptor. function paintFor(ctx, fill) { const p = fill.value; switch (fill.tag) { case "Flat": return cssColor(p); case "Span": // Brush.shade's t is 1 when the edges meet, all the way from the middle // colour to the edge colour. if (p.right_x === p.left_x) return cssColor(mix(p.middle_color, p.edge_color, 1)); return withStops(ctx.createLinearGradient(p.left_x, 0, p.right_x, 0), [[0, cssColor(p.edge_color)], [0.5, cssColor(p.middle_color)], [1, cssColor(p.edge_color)]]); case "Radial": // With no ring to walk, Brush.shade mixes all the way to the outer colour. if (!(p.outer_radius > p.inner_radius)) return cssColor(mix(p.inner_color, p.outer_color, 1)); return withStops(ctx.createRadialGradient(p.center.x, p.center.y, p.inner_radius, p.center.x, p.center.y, p.outer_radius), [[0, cssColor(p.inner_color)], [1, cssColor(p.outer_color)]]); case "Linear": { const dx = p.end_point.x - p.start_point.x; const dy = p.end_point.y - p.start_point.y; if (!(dx * dx + dy * dy > 0)) return cssColor(twoStopAt(p.stops, 1)); return withStops(ctx.createLinearGradient(p.start_point.x, p.start_point.y, p.end_point.x, p.end_point.y), twoStops(p.stops)); } case "Glow": // With no ring to walk, Brush.shade takes t = 1, past the middle offset, // and mixes from the middle colour to the outer one. if (!(p.outer_radius > p.inner_radius)) { return cssColor(mix(p.middle_color, p.outer_color, (1 - p.middle_offset) / (1 - p.middle_offset))); } return withStops(ctx.createRadialGradient(p.center.x, p.center.y, p.inner_radius, p.center.x, p.center.y, p.outer_radius), [[0, cssColor(p.inner_color)], [p.middle_offset, cssColor(p.middle_color)], [1, cssColor(p.outer_color)]]); case "Ellipse": return { ellipse: p }; default: throw new Error(`shapes_canvas: no brush ${fill.tag}`); } } // An ellipse brush carries its axes, the matrix that takes the unit circle to // the ellipse, which is the transform a canvas wants. function fillThroughEllipse(ctx, p) { ctx.save(); ctx.clip(); ctx.transform(p.axis_u.x, p.axis_u.y, p.axis_v.x, p.axis_v.y, p.center.x, p.center.y); ctx.fillStyle = withStops(ctx.createRadialGradient(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1), twoStops(p.stops)); ctx.fillRect(-1e4, -1e4, 2e4, 2e4); // clipped to the path; past r=1 the gradient holds ctx.restore(); } function fillShape(ctx, fill) { const paint = paintFor(ctx, fill); if (paint.ellipse) fillThroughEllipse(ctx, paint.ellipse); else { ctx.fillStyle = paint; ctx.fill(); } } // A triangle, a quad and a polygon are traced alike, as the path round their // corners in order. function tracePolygon(ctx, corners) { ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(corners[0].x, corners[0].y); for (let i = 1; i < corners.length; i++) ctx.lineTo(corners[i].x, corners[i].y); ctx.closePath(); } // Where the shapes after a view mark are: the camera written as the matrix a // canvas takes. Camera.world_to_screen does this in Roc, BeginMode2D in raylib. // `scale` is how many canvas pixels the app's own pixel takes. function setSpace(ctx, space, scale) { if (space.tag === "Screen") { ctx.setTransform(scale, 0, 0, scale, 0, 0); return; } const c = space.value; const radians = (c.rotation * Math.PI) / 180; const cos = Math.cos(radians) * c.zoom; const sin = Math.sin(radians) * c.zoom; ctx.setTransform(scale * cos, scale * sin, -scale * sin, scale * cos, scale * (c.offset.x - (c.target.x * cos - c.target.y * sin)), scale * (c.offset.y - (c.target.x * sin + c.target.y * cos))); } // The viewer's own typefaces. A stack names the best face on each common system // and ends in the generic family, so a page loads no font and always finds one. const TYPEFACES = { Prose: 'system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif', Code: 'ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, "DejaVu Sans Mono", "Liberation Mono", monospace', }; const TEXT_ALIGN = { Left: 'left', Center: 'center' }; function paintText(ctx, p) { ctx.font = `${p.size}px ${TYPEFACES[p.face.tag]}`; ctx.textAlign = TEXT_ALIGN[p.align.tag]; ctx.textBaseline = 'alphabetic'; ctx.fillStyle = cssColor(p.color); ctx.fillText(p.text, p.x, p.y); } const scratch = { canvas: null, ctx: null }; function paintImage(ctx, p) { if (!p.cols || !p.rows) return; if (!scratch.canvas) { scratch.canvas = document.createElement('canvas'); scratch.ctx = scratch.canvas.getContext('2d'); } if (scratch.canvas.width !== p.cols || scratch.canvas.height !== p.rows) { scratch.canvas.width = Number(p.cols); scratch.canvas.height = Number(p.rows); } const image = scratch.ctx.createImageData(Number(p.cols), Number(p.rows)); const bytes = image.data; for (let i = 0; i < p.pixels.length; i++) { const c = p.pixels[i]; bytes[i * 4] = channel(c.r); bytes[i * 4 + 1] = channel(c.g); bytes[i * 4 + 2] = channel(c.b); bytes[i * 4 + 3] = channel(c.a * 255); } scratch.ctx.putImageData(image, 0, 0); const smoothing = ctx.imageSmoothingEnabled; ctx.imageSmoothingEnabled = false; ctx.drawImage(scratch.canvas, 0, 0, Number(p.cols), Number(p.rows), p.x, p.y, p.width, p.height); ctx.imageSmoothingEnabled = smoothing; } function paintFrame(ctx, shapes, scale = 1) { for (const shape of shapes) { const p = shape.value; switch (shape.tag) { // The two marks are not shapes: one says how the shapes after it // combine, the other says where they are. case "Blend": ctx.globalCompositeOperation = p.tag === "Add" ? 'lighter' : 'source-over'; break; case "View": setSpace(ctx, p, scale); break; case "Image": paintImage(ctx, p); break; case "Text": paintText(ctx, p); break; case "Triangle": tracePolygon(ctx, [p.first, p.second, p.third]); fillShape(ctx, p.fill); break; case "Quad": tracePolygon(ctx, [p.first, p.second, p.third, p.fourth]); fillShape(ctx, p.fill); break; case "Polygon": tracePolygon(ctx, p.corners); fillShape(ctx, p.fill); break; case "Disc": ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(p.center.x, p.center.y, p.radius, 0, Math.PI * 2); ctx.closePath(); fillShape(ctx, p.fill); break; default: throw new Error(`shapes_canvas: no shape ${shape.tag}`); } } ctx.globalCompositeOperation = 'source-over'; ctx.setTransform(scale, 0, 0, scale, 0, 0); } const ShapesCanvas = { paint: paintFrame };

name: canvas_apps/web/mini_font.mjs
html: // mini_font reads the outlines of letters out of a TrueType file, so that // mini_canvas can set a line of type the way a browser does. // // A browser picks the first face of a stack that its machine has. This picks a // face that stands in for the stack's generic family, from fonts on this // machine, so a shot shows type of about the size and color the viewer gets, but // not their exact letters. It reads what those files use, and a file it can't // read, or a letter the face lacks, stops the shot. import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs'; const STAND_INS = { 'sans-serif': '/usr/share/fonts/truetype/liberation/LiberationSans-Regular.ttf', monospace: '/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSansMono.ttf', }; const CURVE_STEPS = 6; // A composite glyph's flags, from the `glyf` table's format. const WORDS = 1, SCALE = 8, MORE = 32, XY_SCALE = 64, TWO_BY_TWO = 128; class TrueType { constructor(path) { const file = readFileSync(path); this.view = new DataView(file.buffer, file.byteOffset, file.byteLength); this.tables = {}; const count = this.view.getUint16(4); for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) { const at = 12 + i * 16; this.tables[file.toString('latin1', at, at + 4)] = this.view.getUint32(at + 8); } for (const name of ['cmap', 'glyf', 'head', 'hhea', 'hmtx', 'loca']) { if (!(name in this.tables)) throw new Error(`mini_font: ${path} has no ${name} table`); } this.path = path; this.unitsPerEm = this.view.getUint16(this.tables.head + 18); this.longOffsets = this.view.getInt16(this.tables.head + 50) === 1; this.metrics = this.view.getUint16(this.tables.hhea + 34); this.cmap = this.unicodeSubtable(); } // The format 4 subtable, which covers the Basic Multilingual Plane. unicodeSubtable() { const v = this.view, base = this.tables.cmap; const count = v.getUint16(base + 2); for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) { const at = base + v.getUint32(base + 8 + i * 8); if (v.getUint16(at) === 4) return at; } throw new Error(`mini_font: ${this.path} has no format 4 cmap`); } glyphOf(codePoint) { const v = this.view, at = this.cmap; const twice = v.getUint16(at + 6); const ends = at + 14, starts = ends + twice + 2, deltas = starts + twice, offsets = deltas + twice; for (let i = 0; i < twice; i += 2) { if (codePoint > v.getUint16(ends + i)) continue; const first = v.getUint16(starts + i); if (codePoint < first) break; const delta = v.getUint16(deltas + i), offset = v.getUint16(offsets + i); if (offset === 0) return (codePoint + delta) & 0xffff; const glyph = v.getUint16(offsets + i + offset + (codePoint - first) * 2); if (glyph !== 0) return (glyph + delta) & 0xffff; break; } throw new Error(`mini_font: ${this.path} has no letter U+${codePoint.toString(16)}`); } advanceOf(glyph) { return this.view.getUint16(this.tables.hmtx + Math.min(glyph, this.metrics - 1) * 4); } // Where a glyph's record is, or null for one with no outline, like a space. recordOf(glyph) { const v = this.view, loca = this.tables.loca; const start = this.longOffsets ? v.getUint32(loca + glyph * 4) : v.getUint16(loca + glyph * 2) * 2; const end = this.longOffsets ? v.getUint32(loca + glyph * 4 + 4) : v.getUint16(loca + glyph * 2 + 2) * 2; return start === end ? null : this.tables.glyf + start; } // A glyph's contours in font units, y up: lists of { x, y, on }. contoursOf(glyph) { const at = this.recordOf(glyph); if (at === null) return []; const contours = this.view.getInt16(at); return contours >= 0 ? this.simple(at + 10, contours) : this.composite(at + 10); } simple(start, contours) { const v = this.view; let at = start; const lastPoints = []; for (let i = 0; i < contours; i++, at += 2) lastPoints.push(v.getUint16(at)); const count = contours ? lastPoints[contours - 1] + 1 : 0; at += 2 + v.getUint16(at); const flags = []; while (flags.length < count) { const flag = v.getUint8(at++); flags.push(flag); if (flag & 8) for (let n = v.getUint8(at++); n > 0; n--) flags.push(flag); } // A coordinate is a change from the last one: a byte with its sign in a // flag, or else a word, or nothing when the flag says it is the same. const readAxis = (short, same) => { const values = []; let value = 0; for (const flag of flags) { if (flag & short) { const d = v.getUint8(at++); value += flag & same ? d : -d; } else if (!(flag & same)) { value += v.getInt16(at); at += 2; } values.push(value); } return values; }; const xs = readAxis(2, 16); const ys = readAxis(4, 32); const out = []; let first = 0; for (const last of lastPoints) { const contour = []; for (let i = first; i <= last; i++) contour.push({ x: xs[i], y: ys[i], on: (flags[i] & 1) === 1 }); out.push(contour); first = last + 1; } return out; } composite(start) { const v = this.view; const out = []; let at = start, flags; do { flags = v.getUint16(at); const part = v.getUint16(at + 2); at += 4; const dx = flags & WORDS ? v.getInt16(at) : v.getInt8(at); const dy = flags & WORDS ? v.getInt16(at + 2) : v.getInt8(at + 1); at += flags & WORDS ? 4 : 2; if (flags & (SCALE | XY_SCALE | TWO_BY_TWO)) throw new Error(`mini_font: ${this.path} scales a glyph's part`); for (const contour of this.contoursOf(part)) { out.push(contour.map((p) => ({ ...p, x: p.x + dx, y: p.y + dy }))); } } while (flags & MORE); return out; } } // One contour as straight lines. Two curve points in a row have an unwritten // point on the curve halfway between them. function flatten(contour) { const points = []; contour.forEach((p, i) => { const next = contour[(i + 1) % contour.length]; points.push(p); if (!p.on && !next.on) points.push({ x: (p.x + next.x) / 2, y: (p.y + next.y) / 2, on: true }); }); const start = points.findIndex((p) => p.on); const ring = [...points.slice(start), ...points.slice(0, start)]; const out = []; ring.forEach((p, i) => { if (!p.on) return; out.push([p.x, p.y]); const control = ring[(i + 1) % ring.length]; if (control.on) return; const end = ring[(i + 2) % ring.length]; for (let step = 1; step < CURVE_STEPS; step++) { const t = step / CURVE_STEPS, u = 1 - t; out.push([u * u * p.x + 2 * u * t * control.x + t * t * end.x, u * u * p.y + 2 * u * t * control.y + t * t * end.y]); } }); return out; } const fonts = new Map(); function fontFor(path) { if (!fonts.has(path)) fonts.set(path, new TrueType(path)); return fonts.get(path); } // What a canvas's `font` string asks for: a size in pixels, then a stack. export function faceOf(fontText) { const asked = fontText.match(/^([0-9.]+)px (.+)$/); if (!asked) throw new Error(`mini_font: cannot read the font ${fontText}`); const generic = asked[2].split(',').pop().trim(); if (!(generic in STAND_INS)) throw new Error(`mini_font: no face for ${generic}`); const font = fontFor(STAND_INS[generic]); const scale = Number(asked[1]) / font.unitsPerEm; return { // Contours of [x, y] in pixels, y down, from the line's left end on its // baseline, and the line's width. outline(text) { const contours = []; let pen = 0; for (const letter of text) { const glyph = font.glyphOf(letter.codePointAt(0)); for (const contour of font.contoursOf(glyph)) { contours.push(flatten(contour).map(([x, y]) => [pen + x * scale, -y * scale])); } pen += font.advanceOf(glyph) * scale; } return { contours, width: pen }; }, }; }

html: #!/usr/bin/env node // This checks what a canvas gets asked for a line of type, on both sides of // each choice a `Text` shape makes, and that a page scaled for the screen still // puts things where the app said. It hands shapes_canvas.js shapes in the form // the generated reader answers. // // With `raster`, it also sets lines of type on mini_canvas and looks at the // ink, which needs the stand-in fonts that mini_font.mjs names. build.sh gives // that to the widgets, whose shots need those fonts anyway. // // node canvas_apps/web/text_check.mjs [raster] import { readFileSync } from "node:fs"; import vm from "node:vm"; const here = new URL(".", import.meta.url).pathname; function fail(why) { console.error(`text_check: ${why}`); process.exit(1); } function same(got, want, what) { if (JSON.stringify(got) !== JSON.stringify(want)) { fail(`${what}: got ${JSON.stringify(got)}, want ${JSON.stringify(want)}`); } } const sandbox = { Math, Error, Array, Uint32Array, Float32Array, DataView }; vm.createContext(sandbox); vm.runInContext(`${readFileSync(`${here}shapes_canvas.js`, "utf8")}\nglobalThis.wire = ShapesCanvas;`, sandbox); // What a frame did to the canvas: each call, and each property as it stood when // the line was set. function painted(shapes, scale) { const calls = []; const set = {}; const ctx = new Proxy({}, { get: (_t, k) => (...a) => { calls.push({ k, a, ...set }); }, set: (_t, k, v) => { set[k] = v; return true; }, }); sandbox.wire.paint(ctx, shapes, scale); return calls; } const line = (fields) => ({ tag: "Text", value: { text: "Sun.height_px(clock)", x: 24, y: 266, size: 15, face: { tag: "Code" }, align: { tag: "Left" }, color: { r: 32, g: 16, b: 8, a: 1 }, ...fields, }, }); const setting = (fields) => painted([line(fields)]).find((call) => call.k === "fillText"); const code = setting({}); same(code.a, ["Sun.height_px(clock)", 24, 266], "the words and their place"); same(code.fillStyle, "rgba(32,16,8,1)", "the color"); same(code.textBaseline, "alphabetic", "the baseline"); same(code.textAlign, "left", "a left-aligned line"); if (!code.font.startsWith("15px ") || !code.font.endsWith(", monospace")) fail(`code is set in ${code.font}`); const prose = setting({ face: { tag: "Prose" }, align: { tag: "Center" }, size: 13.5 }); same(prose.textAlign, "center", "a centered line"); if (!prose.font.startsWith("13.5px ") || !prose.font.endsWith(", sans-serif")) fail(`prose is set in ${prose.font}`); // Text is not a mark: the frame's end is the one transform this frame sets. const transforms = (scale, shapes) => painted(shapes, scale).filter((c) => c.k === "setTransform").map((c) => c.a); same(transforms(undefined, [line({})]), [[1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0]], "a frame at the app's own size"); same(transforms(2.5, [line({})]), [[2.5, 0, 0, 2.5, 0, 0]], "a frame scaled for the screen"); // A view is the app's own, so a scaled page holds the scale outside it. const camera = { target: { x: 10, y: 20 }, offset: { x: 100, y: 200 }, rotation: 0, zoom: 3 }; const view = { tag: "View", value: { tag: "World", value: camera } }; same(transforms(1, [view])[0], [3, 0, -0, 3, 70, 140], "a view at the app's own size"); same(transforms(2, [view])[0], [6, 0, -0, 6, 140, 280], "a view scaled for the screen"); same(transforms(2, [{ tag: "View", value: { tag: "Screen" } }])[0], [2, 0, 0, 2, 0, 0], "the screen, scaled"); let raster = ""; if (process.argv[2] === "raster") { const { createCanvas } = await import("./mini_canvas.mjs"); const stack = (generic) => `20px Nothing Here, ${generic}`; // The ink's left and right ends, and its top and bottom, in canvas pixels. const ink = (paint) => { const canvas = createCanvas(200, 60); const ctx = canvas.getContext("2d"); ctx.fillStyle = "#fff"; ctx.fillRect(0, 0, 200, 60); ctx.fillStyle = "#000"; paint(ctx); const inked = []; for (let y = 0; y < 60; y++) { for (let x = 0; x < 200; x++) if (canvas.pixel(x, y)[0] < 128) inked.push({ x, y }); } if (!inked.length) fail("a line of type left no ink"); const xs = inked.map((p) => p.x), ys = inked.map((p) => p.y); return { left: Math.min(...xs), right: Math.max(...xs), top: Math.min(...ys), bottom: Math.max(...ys), count: inked.length }; }; const set = (font, align, text) => ink((ctx) => { ctx.font = font; ctx.textAlign = align; ctx.fillText(text, 100, 40); }); // A capital stands on the baseline, about 0.7 of the size tall. const capital = set(stack("sans-serif"), "left", "H"); if (capital.bottom !== 39) fail(`a capital ends at row ${capital.bottom}, not on the baseline`); if (capital.top < 24 || capital.top > 27) fail(`a capital's top is at row ${capital.top}`); if (capital.left < 100 || capital.left > 104) fail(`a line starts at column ${capital.left}`); // A centered line sits either side of its x. const centered = set(stack("sans-serif"), "center", "HHH"); if (centered.left >= 100 || centered.right <= 100) fail(`a centered line runs ${centered.left} to ${centered.right}`); if (Math.abs(100 - centered.left - (centered.right - 100)) > 2) fail("a centered line is off center"); // In monospace an i is as wide as an m; in a sans serif it is narrower. const wide = (generic, text) => { const r = set(stack(generic), "left", `${text}|`); return r.right; }; if (wide("monospace", "iiii") !== wide("monospace", "mmmm")) fail("the monospace stand-in isn't monospace"); if (wide("sans-serif", "iiii") >= wide("sans-serif", "mmmm")) fail("the sans stand-in isn't proportional"); // A letter with a hole keeps it: an o inks far less than its box. const ring = set(stack("sans-serif"), "left", "o"); if (ring.count * 10 > (ring.right - ring.left + 1) * (ring.bottom - ring.top + 1) * 7) fail("an o has no hole"); // A stack with no generic family, and a letter no face has, stop the shot. for (const [font, text] of [["20px Nothing Here", "H"], ["20px sans-serif", "\u{e000}"]]) { let stopped = false; try { set(font, "left", text); } catch { stopped = true; } if (!stopped) fail(`${font} set ${text} and should have stopped`); } raster = ", and type on mini_canvas"; } console.log(`text_check: lines of type and scaled frames as asked${raster}`);

name: canvas_apps/widget_kit/embed.js
html: // embed.js sits a canvas app's page inside a page of prose. Each app stays an // ordinary page of its own, served beside the prose and shown in an iframe: // // <iframe class="canvas-app" src="../sky_widget/" loading="lazy" // style="aspect-ratio: 640 / 360"></iframe> // <script src="embed.js"></script> // // canvas_app_runner.js lays a page out for a whole window and listens for the // wheel, and neither suits a frame in a column of text. This reaches into each // frame, which is on the same origin, and changes four things. The canvas // fills the frame. The wheel goes on scrolling the prose, since no widget reads // it. A click hands the frame the keyboard, because the runner's pointerdown // cancels the browser's own focusing. A frame off the screen stops, because a // browser goes on running a same-origin frame it can't see, and a page of // these would keep a core busy. const FILL_THE_FRAME = ` body { height: auto !important; background: none !important; display: block !important; } canvas { display: block !important; width: 100% !important; height: auto !important; max-width: none !important; max-height: none !important; } `; // The runner asks for each animation frame in turn, so holding back one answer // stops it, and the runner's own cap on catching up covers the time away. function stopWhileOffScreen(frame) { const view = frame.contentWindow; const askBrowser = view.requestAnimationFrame.bind(view); let onScreen = true; let waiting = null; view.requestAnimationFrame = (callback) => { if (onScreen) return askBrowser(callback); waiting = callback; return 0; }; new IntersectionObserver(([sighting]) => { onScreen = sighting.isIntersecting; if (onScreen && waiting) { askBrowser(waiting); waiting = null; } }).observe(frame); } function fitFrame(frame) { const view = frame.contentWindow; const style = view.document.createElement('style'); style.textContent = FILL_THE_FRAME; view.document.head.append(style); view.addEventListener('wheel', (event) => event.stopImmediatePropagation(), { capture: true }); view.addEventListener('pointerdown', () => view.focus()); } for (const frame of document.querySelectorAll('iframe.canvas-app')) { frame.addEventListener('load', () => { fitFrame(frame); stopWhileOffScreen(frame); }); }

name: canvas_apps/safari/tutorial/book.js
html: // The Safari Ride book's one script for every page. A table may run as wide as // the page allows, and a column of sentences then makes lines too long to // read, so this marks each column that holds prose and book.css wraps it at a // reading width. A column holds prose when its cells average more than // PROSE_LENGTH characters, as an Explanation column does and a column of names // does not. const PROSE_LENGTH = 60; for (const table of document.querySelectorAll("article table")) { const rows = [...table.rows]; const columns = Math.max(...rows.map((row) => row.cells.length)); for (let column = 0; column < columns; column++) { const cells = rows.map((row) => row.cells[column]).filter((cell) => cell); const body = cells.filter((cell) => cell.tagName === "TD"); if (body.length === 0) continue; const average = body.reduce((sum, cell) => sum + cell.textContent.trim().length, 0) / body.length; if (average > PROSE_LENGTH) { for (const cell of cells) cell.classList.add("prose"); } } }

html: // shapewire — painting a frame onto a canvas. // // EXPERIMENT: the decoder that used to be the first half of this file is GONE. // The platform declares `frame : Box(model) -> List(Frame.Shape)`, so the // compiler's own type table carries the vocabulary and `roc_glue.js` — which // `roc glue` generates from it — reads a frame. What is left here is what a // canvas does with one, which no generator can know. // // It answers one name, `ShapeWire`, with `paint`. const stopAt = (offset, floor = 0) => Math.max(floor, Math.min(1, offset)); const channel = (v) => Math.max(0, Math.min(255, Math.round(v))); const cssColor = (c) => `rgba(${channel(c.r)},${channel(c.g)},${channel(c.b)},${c.a})`; const withStops = (gradient, stops) => { stops.forEach(([offset, color]) => gradient.addColorStop(offset, color)); return gradient; }; // A fill becomes something canvas can paint with. An ellipse is the exception: // it paints through a transform, so it stays a descriptor. function paintFor(ctx, fill) { const p = fill.value; switch (fill.tag) { case "Skip": return null; case "Flat": return cssColor(p); case "Span": return withStops(ctx.createLinearGradient(p.x0, 0, p.x1, 0), [[0, cssColor(p.edge)], [0.5, cssColor(p.middle)], [1, cssColor(p.edge)]]); case "Radial": if (!(p.r1 > p.r0)) return cssColor(p.outer); return withStops(ctx.createRadialGradient(p.x, p.y, p.r0, p.x, p.y, p.r1), [[0, cssColor(p.inner)], [1, cssColor(p.outer)]]); case "Linear": return withStops(ctx.createLinearGradient(p.ax, p.ay, p.ax + p.dx, p.ay + p.dy), [[stopAt(p.o0), cssColor(p.c0)], [stopAt(p.o1, stopAt(p.o0)), cssColor(p.c1)]]); case "Glow": // Brush.shade and BrushGlsl both end at c2 when there is no ring to walk. if (!(p.r1 > p.r0)) return cssColor(p.c2); return withStops(ctx.createRadialGradient(p.x, p.y, p.r0, p.x, p.y, p.r1), [[0, cssColor(p.c0)], [0.4, cssColor(p.c1)], [1, cssColor(p.c2)]]); case "Ellipse": return { ellipse: p }; default: throw new Error(`shapewire: no brush ${fill.tag}`); } } // An ellipse brush carries the matrix that takes a scene offset TO the unit // circle; a canvas wants the one that goes the other way, so it is inverted. function fillThroughEllipse(ctx, p) { const det = p.ia * p.id - p.ib * p.ic; if (Math.abs(det) < 1e-4) { ctx.fillStyle = cssColor(p.c0); ctx.fill(); return; } ctx.save(); ctx.clip(); ctx.transform(p.id / det, -p.ic / det, -p.ib / det, p.ia / det, p.x, p.y); ctx.fillStyle = withStops(ctx.createRadialGradient(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1), [[stopAt(p.o0), cssColor(p.c0)], [stopAt(p.o1, stopAt(p.o0)), cssColor(p.c1)]]); ctx.fillRect(-1e4, -1e4, 2e4, 2e4); // clipped to the path; past r=1 the gradient holds ctx.restore(); } function fillShape(ctx, fill) { const paint = paintFor(ctx, fill); if (paint === null) return; if (paint.ellipse) fillThroughEllipse(ctx, paint.ellipse); else { ctx.fillStyle = paint; ctx.fill(); } } function tracePoly(ctx, pts) { ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(pts[0], pts[1]); for (let i = 2; i < pts.length; i += 2) ctx.lineTo(pts[i], pts[i + 1]); ctx.closePath(); } // Where the shapes after a view mark are: the camera written as the matrix a // canvas takes. Camera.world_to_screen does this in Roc, BeginMode2D in raylib. function setSpace(ctx, space) { if (space.tag === "Screen") { ctx.setTransform(1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0); return; } const c = space.value; const radians = (c.rotation * Math.PI) / 180; const cos = Math.cos(radians) * c.zoom; const sin = Math.sin(radians) * c.zoom; ctx.setTransform(cos, sin, -sin, cos, c.offset.x - (c.target.x * cos - c.target.y * sin), c.offset.y - (c.target.x * sin + c.target.y * cos)); } const scratch = { canvas: null, ctx: null }; function paintImage(ctx, p) { if (!p.cols || !p.rows) return; if (!scratch.canvas) { scratch.canvas = document.createElement('canvas'); scratch.ctx = scratch.canvas.getContext('2d'); } if (scratch.canvas.width !== p.cols || scratch.canvas.height !== p.rows) { scratch.canvas.width = Number(p.cols); scratch.canvas.height = Number(p.rows); } const image = scratch.ctx.createImageData(Number(p.cols), Number(p.rows)); const bytes = image.data; for (let i = 0; i < p.pixels.length; i++) { const c = p.pixels[i]; bytes[i * 4] = channel(c.r); bytes[i * 4 + 1] = channel(c.g); bytes[i * 4 + 2] = channel(c.b); bytes[i * 4 + 3] = channel(c.a * 255); } scratch.ctx.putImageData(image, 0, 0); const smoothing = ctx.imageSmoothingEnabled; ctx.imageSmoothingEnabled = false; ctx.drawImage(scratch.canvas, 0, 0, Number(p.cols), Number(p.rows), p.x, p.y, p.w, p.h); ctx.imageSmoothingEnabled = smoothing; } function paintFrame(ctx, shapes) { for (const shape of shapes) { const p = shape.value; switch (shape.tag) { // The two marks are not shapes: one says how the shapes after it // combine, the other says where they are. case "Blend": ctx.globalCompositeOperation = p.tag === "Add" ? 'lighter' : 'source-over'; break; case "View": setSpace(ctx, p); break; case "Image": paintImage(ctx, p); break; case "Poly": tracePoly(ctx, p.pts); fillShape(ctx, p.fill); break; case "Rect": ctx.beginPath(); ctx.rect(p.x, p.y, p.w, p.h); ctx.closePath(); fillShape(ctx, p.fill); break; case "Disc": if (p.clip.tag === "Within") { const r = p.clip.value; ctx.save(); ctx.beginPath(); ctx.rect(r.x, r.y, r.w, r.h); ctx.clip(); } ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(p.x, p.y, p.r, 0, Math.PI * 2); ctx.closePath(); fillShape(ctx, p.fill); if (p.clip.tag === "Within") ctx.restore(); break; default: throw new Error(`shapewire: a page is never sent ${shape.tag}`); } } ctx.globalCompositeOperation = 'source-over'; ctx.setTransform(1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0); } const ShapeWire = { paint: paintFrame };

html: // **THE PLAYGROUND'S PAGE**: markdown on the left, the package's render on // the right, as you type. The canned examples are the judge's // (examples.jsonl, beside the page); choosing one loads its source into the // editor, where it is yours to change. // // **ONLY THE RENDERER'S HTML IS INSERTED AS HTML**, into #preview: it is what // the chat would show. Everything else the page writes (captions, the html // source, the answers, a refusal, an error) is text. import { load } from "./md_wasm.js"; const $ = (id) => { const e = document.getElementById(id); if (!e) throw new Error(`the page has no #${id}`); return e; }; // Typing renders after this pause; choosing an example or a mode, at once. const TYPING_MS = 60; async function fetched(path, how) { const r = await fetch(path); if (!r.ok) throw new Error(`${path}: ${r.status}`); return how === "bytes" ? r.arrayBuffer() : r.text(); } function parseExamples(jsonl) { return jsonl.split("\n").filter((l) => l !== "").map((l) => JSON.parse(l)); } async function main() { const [wasm, jsonl] = await Promise.all([fetched("md.wasm", "bytes"), fetched("examples.jsonl", "text")]); const md = await load(wasm); const examples = parseExamples(jsonl); const source = $("source"), preview = $("preview"), html = $("html"); const menu = $("example"), caption = $("caption"), showSource = $("show-source"); const units = $("units"), hostility = $("hostility"), error = $("error"), refusal = $("refusal"); const modes = [...document.querySelectorAll('input[name="mode"]')]; for (const ex of examples) { const o = document.createElement("option"); o.value = ex.id; o.textContent = ex.id; menu.appendChild(o); } const edited = document.createElement("option"); edited.value = ""; edited.textContent = "(your own)"; menu.appendChild(edited); const mode = () => (modes.find((m) => m.checked) || modes[0]).value; function render() { let got; try { got = md.answer(source.value, mode()); } catch (e) { preview.innerHTML = ""; html.textContent = ""; units.textContent = hostility.textContent = ""; refusal.hidden = true; error.textContent = `the renderer failed: ${e && e.message || e}`; error.hidden = false; return; } error.hidden = true; // The chat refuses a hostile message whole (a 400 with these words), so // in chat mode the page shows the refusal, not a render. The trusted // modes have no budget: their caller decides for itself. const refused = mode() === "chat" && got.hostile !== ""; refusal.hidden = !refused; refusal.textContent = refused ? `Refused: the chat posts none of this message ("${got.hostile}").` : ""; preview.innerHTML = refused ? "" : got.html; html.textContent = refused ? "" : got.html; units.textContent = String(got.workUnits); hostility.textContent = got.hostile === "" ? "Renderable" : `TooMuchFormatting: the chat says "${got.hostile}"`; hostility.className = got.hostile === "" ? "" : "hostile"; } function choose(id) { const ex = examples.find((e) => e.id === id); if (!ex) return; menu.value = ex.id; caption.textContent = ex.caption; source.value = ex.md; render(); } let pending = null; source.addEventListener("input", () => { // Changed from an example: still shown, its caption no longer the text's. if (menu.value !== "" && examples.find((e) => e.id === menu.value)?.md !== source.value) { menu.value = ""; caption.textContent = ""; } clearTimeout(pending); pending = setTimeout(render, TYPING_MS); }); menu.addEventListener("change", () => choose(menu.value)); for (const m of modes) m.addEventListener("change", render); showSource.addEventListener("change", () => { html.hidden = !showSource.checked; preview.hidden = showSource.checked; }); const wanted = decodeURIComponent((globalThis.location?.hash || "").slice(1)); choose(examples.some((e) => e.id === wanted) ? wanted : examples[0].id); return { examples, choose, render }; } // The page's run, as a promise a test can wait on. globalThis.playground = main().catch((e) => { const el = document.getElementById("error"); if (el) { el.textContent = `the playground did not start: ${e && e.message || e}`; el.hidden = false; } throw e; });

name: site/live/markdown/md_wasm.js
html: // **THE RENDERER'S DOOR** (md.wasm, built from playground/answer.roc on // playground/platform/): one call, `answer(md, mode)`, the package's three // answers for a message. The page and the test (check.mjs) both come through // here, so the test holds the page's own seam to the judge's answers. // // The bytes cross through the wasm's memory: `input(len)` hands back where to // write the message's UTF-8, `answer(len, mode)` renders it, and each answer // is read out by `partPtr(k)` and `partLen(k)`, valid until the next call. export const MODES = ["chat", "trusted", "reflow"]; const encoder = new TextEncoder(); const decoder = new TextDecoder("utf-8", { fatal: true }); // The wasm's bytes, instantiated; its four exports wrapped. export async function load(bytes) { const { instance } = await WebAssembly.instantiate(bytes, {}); const x = instance.exports; for (const name of ["memory", "input", "answer", "partPtr", "partLen"]) { if (!(name in x)) throw new Error(`md.wasm does not export ${name}`); } const answer = (md, mode) => { const m = MODES.indexOf(mode); if (m < 0) throw new Error(`no mode ${mode}`); const text = encoder.encode(md); const at = x.input(text.length); new Uint8Array(x.memory.buffer, at, text.length).set(text); const n = x.answer(text.length, m); if (n !== 3) throw new Error(`md.wasm gave ${n} answers, not 3`); // The memory may have grown during the call: a fresh view each read. const part = (k) => decoder.decode(new Uint8Array(x.memory.buffer, x.partPtr(k), x.partLen(k))); return { html: part(0), workUnits: Number(part(1)), hostile: part(2) }; }; return { answer }; }

html: // The way home, and the dev channel's banner, for every page of Steve's Roc // Apps. A page loads it with one line, the path relative to the page: // // <script src="../shared/home.js"></script> // // The site's root is the directory above this script, so a page at any depth, // on any host, links to its own channel's landing page. Only the dev root holds // a `channel` file, and a page there shows a banner naming it; staging and prod // serve the same files and show none. The landing page loads it too, and gets // the banner without the link. (() => { const root = new URL('..', document.currentScript.src); const pill = 'padding:3px 8px;border-radius:4px;color:#fff;text-decoration:none;pointer-events:auto'; const bar = document.createElement('div'); bar.style.cssText = 'position:fixed;top:6px;right:6px;z-index:2147483647;display:flex;gap:6px;' + 'font:12px/1.4 system-ui,sans-serif;pointer-events:none'; if (new URL('.', location.href).href !== root.href) { const home = document.createElement('a'); home.href = root.href; home.textContent = "Steve's Roc Apps"; home.style.cssText = pill + ';background:rgba(24,24,24,.72)'; bar.append(home); } const show = () => document.body.append(bar); document.body ? show() : document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', show); fetch(new URL('channel', root)).then(r => (r.ok ? r.text() : '')).then(text => { const channel = text.trim(); if (!channel) return; const banner = document.createElement('span'); banner.textContent = channel; banner.style.cssText = pill + ';background:#b3261e'; bar.prepend(banner); }).catch(() => {}); })();

name: site/squeeze_png.mjs
html: // squeeze_png.mjs rewrites an 8-bit RGB or RGBA PNG as a small RGB one, the // same pixels with the alpha dropped. roc-screensaver's native harness writes // its frames uncompressed (a 960 by 600 frame is 1.7 MB), and a landing page's // picture should be a few tens of kilobytes. Each row takes whichever of PNG's // five filters leaves the smallest sum, the usual heuristic, and the rows are // deflated at level 9. site/publish_screensavers.shale runs it. // // node site/squeeze_png.mjs <in.png> <out.png> import { readFileSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs"; import zlib from "node:zlib"; const [from, to] = process.argv.slice(2); if (!from || !to) { console.error("usage: squeeze_png.mjs <in.png> <out.png>"); process.exit(2); } const png = readFileSync(from); let at = 8; let width = 0, height = 0, channels = 0; const idat = []; while (at < png.length) { const length = png.readUInt32BE(at); const type = png.toString("ascii", at + 4, at + 8); const data = png.subarray(at + 8, at + 8 + length); if (type === "IHDR") { width = data.readUInt32BE(0); height = data.readUInt32BE(4); if (data[8] !== 8 || (data[9] !== 2 && data[9] !== 6) || data[12] !== 0) { console.error(`${from}: only 8-bit RGB or RGBA, not interlaced (depth ${data[8]}, colour type ${data[9]}, interlace ${data[12]})`); process.exit(1); } channels = data[9] === 2 ? 3 : 4; } if (type === "IDAT") idat.push(data); at += 12 + length; } const packed = zlib.inflateSync(Buffer.concat(idat)); const stride = width * channels; if (packed.length !== height * (stride + 1)) { console.error(`${from}: ${packed.length} bytes of pixels, expected ${height * (stride + 1)}`); process.exit(1); } const paeth = (a, b, c) => { const p = a + b - c, pa = Math.abs(p - a), pb = Math.abs(p - b), pc = Math.abs(p - c); return pa <= pb && pa <= pc ? a : pb <= pc ? b : c; }; // The predictor of filter `f` for byte `i` of a row, `bpp` bytes a pixel. const predict = (f, row, prior, i, bpp) => { const a = i >= bpp ? row[i - bpp] : 0, b = prior[i], c = i >= bpp ? prior[i - bpp] : 0; return [0, a, b, (a + b) >> 1, paeth(a, b, c)][f]; }; // Unfilter into RGB rows. const rgb = Buffer.alloc(height * width * 3); let prior = Buffer.alloc(stride); for (let y = 0; y < height; y++) { const f = packed[y * (stride + 1)]; const row = Buffer.from(packed.subarray(y * (stride + 1) + 1, (y + 1) * (stride + 1))); for (let i = 0; i < stride; i++) row[i] = (row[i] + predict(f, row, prior, i, channels)) & 0xff; for (let x = 0; x < width; x++) row.copy(rgb, (y * width + x) * 3, x * channels, x * channels + 3); prior = row; } // Filter each RGB row by the filter with the smallest sum of signed bytes. const out = Buffer.alloc(height * (width * 3 + 1)); const rowBytes = width * 3; prior = Buffer.alloc(rowBytes); for (let y = 0; y < height; y++) { const row = rgb.subarray(y * rowBytes, (y + 1) * rowBytes); let best = null, bestSum = Infinity, bestF = 0; for (let f = 0; f < 5; f++) { const line = Buffer.alloc(rowBytes); let sum = 0; for (let i = 0; i < rowBytes; i++) { const v = (row[i] - predict(f, row, prior, i, 3)) & 0xff; line[i] = v; sum += v < 128 ? v : 256 - v; } if (sum < bestSum) { best = line; bestSum = sum; bestF = f; } } out[y * (rowBytes + 1)] = bestF; best.copy(out, y * (rowBytes + 1) + 1); prior = row; } const CRC = new Uint32Array(256).map((_, n) => { let c = n; for (let k = 0; k < 8; k++) c = c & 1 ? 0xedb88320 ^ (c >>> 1) : c >>> 1; return c >>> 0; }); const crc32 = (buf) => { let c = 0xffffffff; for (const byte of buf) c = CRC[(c ^ byte) & 0xff] ^ (c >>> 8); return (c ^ 0xffffffff) >>> 0; }; const chunk = (type, data) => { const head = Buffer.alloc(8); head.writeUInt32BE(data.length, 0); head.write(type, 4, "ascii"); const crc = Buffer.alloc(4); crc.writeUInt32BE(crc32(Buffer.concat([head.subarray(4), data])), 0); return Buffer.concat([head, data, crc]); }; const ihdr = Buffer.alloc(13); ihdr.writeUInt32BE(width, 0); ihdr.writeUInt32BE(height, 4); ihdr[8] = 8; ihdr[9] = 2; const squeezed = Buffer.concat([ png.subarray(0, 8), chunk("IHDR", ihdr), chunk("IDAT", zlib.deflateSync(out, { level: 9 })), chunk("IEND", Buffer.alloc(0)), ]); writeFileSync(to, squeezed); console.log(`squeezed ${from}: ${width} by ${height}, ${png.length} bytes to ${squeezed.length}`);

name: fasttrack/web/fasttrack.js
html: // Fast Track's page end: it runs the wasm and draws what Roc says. // // Roc answers the whole page as data (web/platform/Wire.roc), and this knows // nothing about Fast Track. It does two things: // // - **the board is patched.** Its slots come in the same order every time, // so the SVG is built once and afterwards only the attributes that // changed are set; // - **the rest is replaced.** The page's nodes -- a few buttons and lines // -- are rebuilt on every click, with the board's SVG moved into the // node whose tag is "board". // // A click sends back the code Roc gave the thing clicked; nothing here builds // a message. When the computer is playing, the view names a `tick` code, and // the page sends it back by itself after a pause -- one computer click per // tick, so a person can watch. A view's `motions` (what the last click moved) // are walked square by square before the next tick: the board is drawn as red // sees it, so a motion's squares are slot numbers. // // A plain script (the page loads it with <script src>), defining `FastTrack`. // page_check.mjs runs the same file against a stand-in document. const FastTrack = (() => { const SVG = "http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"; // One game in one wasm instance. function game(instance) { const ex = instance.exports; return { start: (millis, setup, seats, teams = 0) => ex.start(millis, setup, seats, teams), click: (code) => ex.update(code), // **computeView FIRST, THEN THE DataView.** Building a view can grow // wasm memory, which detaches every view of the old buffer. view: () => { const at = ex.computeView(); return RocGlue.view(new DataView(ex.memory.buffer), at); }, }; } function board(document) { const svg = document.createElementNS(SVG, "svg"); const labels = document.createElementNS(SVG, "g"); let entries = []; let size = null; function build(slots, onClick) { svg.replaceChildren(); entries = slots.map((s) => { const g = document.createElementNS(SVG, "g"); const shape = document.createElementNS(SVG, s.square ? "rect" : "circle"); const piece = document.createElementNS(SVG, "circle"); g.appendChild(shape); g.appendChild(piece); svg.appendChild(g); const entry = { g, shape, piece, last: null, code: 0 }; g.addEventListener("click", () => { if (entry.code) onClick(entry.code); }); return entry; }); } function set(el, name, value) { el.setAttribute(name, String(value)); } // Only what differs from the last slot at this place is written. function patch(view, onClick) { if (view.board_size !== size) { size = view.board_size; set(svg, "width", size); set(svg, "height", size); } const slots = view.slots; if (entries.length !== slots.length || slots.some((s, i) => entries[i].last && entries[i].last.square !== s.square)) { build(slots, onClick); } slots.forEach((s, i) => { const e = entries[i]; const old = e.last || {}; if (old.cx !== s.cx || old.cy !== s.cy || old.size !== s.size) { if (s.square) { set(e.shape, "x", s.cx - s.size / 2); set(e.shape, "y", s.cy - s.size / 2); set(e.shape, "width", s.size); set(e.shape, "height", s.size); set(e.shape, "rx", 2); } else { set(e.shape, "cx", s.cx); set(e.shape, "cy", s.cy); set(e.shape, "r", s.size / 2); } set(e.piece, "cx", s.cx); set(e.piece, "cy", s.cy); } if (old.fill !== s.fill) set(e.shape, "fill", s.fill); if (old.stroke !== s.stroke) set(e.shape, "stroke", s.stroke); if (old.piece !== s.piece) { set(e.piece, "visibility", s.piece === "" ? "hidden" : "visible"); if (s.piece !== "") { set(e.piece, "fill", s.piece); set(e.piece, "stroke", s.piece); } } if (old.piece_r !== s.piece_r) set(e.piece, "r", s.piece_r); if (old.click !== s.click) set(e.g, "cursor", s.click ? "pointer" : "default"); e.code = s.click; e.last = s; }); // A few words on the board, redrawn every time, above the squares. if (labels.parentNode !== svg) svg.appendChild(labels); labels.replaceChildren(); for (const l of view.labels) { const t = document.createElementNS(SVG, "text"); set(t, "x", l.x); set(t, "y", l.y); set(t, "text-anchor", "middle"); set(t, "font-size", 11); set(t, "fill", l.fill); t.appendChild(document.createTextNode(l.text)); labels.appendChild(t); } } // A piece hidden while a marble walks to it, and shown when it lands. const hide = (i) => entries[i] && set(entries[i].piece, "visibility", "hidden"); const show = (i) => entries[i] && entries[i].last && set(entries[i].piece, "visibility", entries[i].last.piece === "" ?
